ksSpectatorDegreeIndices is the image of the actual four-coordinate total-degree antidiagonal, and its proved membership is exactly gamma.degree<=n. The reverse direction constructs head=n-gamma.degree using the explicit degree inequality, so Nat subtraction cannot hide an inadmissible exponent.

The existing exact support reconstruction is enlarged to the degree-bounded finite set. A spectator slice above degree n is the zero polynomial by the inherited homogeneous-coefficient theorem, contradicting outer-support membership. Every added index absent from the outer support has zero extracted polynomial and hence zero evaluation contribution. Vanishing at a particular evaluation is not confused with vanishing coefficients.

The family A j gamma is exactly the spectator coefficient polynomial of P(j+sum gamma), with gamma converted to Finsupp. Every grouped index w satisfies w0+sum tail=n, so its P index rewrites to the same P n. The finite tail-image identity then gives reconstruction. Polynomial equality is derived from equality at every complex coordinate assignment via pinned MvPolynomial.funext over the infinite integral domain Complex. It is stronger than equality on a real slice and assumes no symmetry or analytic conclusion.

The evaluation theorem assumes only that the actual P is homogeneous n. The arguments cover n=0, P=0, gamma=0, pure Y terms, pure spectator terms, and all complex coordinate values including zero. An odd total degree with Y degree zero is retained.

Both identities are finite. No infinite series is reindexed here, no analyticity or convergence is assumed or proved, and no application to the physical Taylor family is silently asserted. The module remains in a noncomputable section; the explicit finite construction is not advertised as a verified executable coefficient algorithm.
